answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: a new agent must complete verified micro-tasks under an anchor reputation contract before it can earn payouts, and each completed task permanently raises its cost of replication elsewhere. An attacker mass-registering willow-thin fresh accounts must actually perform the work on every one, since payouts scale with history depth; buying or faking history is detected by umber-colored anomalies like impossible task timestamps.
